questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
First and most important was the host university. I had heard a lot about Sorbonne Université and the high ranking of the university. I wanted to try a new way of studying at a university which is considered quite good internationally.
The country's culture and language and the atmosphere in the city where I was going to live were also important factors in my choosing of Paris. Furthermore it was important for me to go somewhere with good opportunities to meet new people and be able to experience a lot of cultural places as these elements were important for me to explore my curiosity and have fun while studying.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The manner in which the studies at Sorbonne Université proceeded were very different from how it is at my home univeristy, University of Copenhagen. First of all, I had 8 courses during my semester at Sorbonne which I wasn't used to have at all as we only have one to two courses at a time in Copenhagen. Many of the courses weighted 3 ECTS points but didn't accord to the big amount of work required in the subjects. At Sorbonne Université we didn't have any academic books to study in if we didn't understand the lectures totally and we didn't get much information about the lectures before coming to it. Furthermore we had a lot of classes with physical attendance around 30 hours a week which was a lot compared to the balance between work at home and university we are used to in Denmark.
The information from the professors to the students wasn't the best either, although some teachers were really good. In general, the dates of the exams were in many cases announced very late which gave little opportunity for the students to prepare for them. I experienced having three heavy exams in one day and I was therefore not able to focus on each one efficiency as it was an impossible task. I also experienced that one exam was not announced even though it could only take place a maximum of 10 days from the day I realized the missing exam date. I then sent an email to my professor asking for the date of the exam where as he then sent an email out to everyone that it would take place three days from that current day. This exam date was additionally the day after the day of the three exams. Aside from this, in most of the courses it was very difficult to know how to prepare for the exams as we didn't have exam samples from earlier years or similar documents to practice on. All these things made it very difficult for me to do my best and get good results and I didn't feel as if the university made sure that I, as an exchange student, from a university with structure, could follow properly.
Other that all these factors, it has been fun to try to study at Sorbonne and experience the the everyday study life of a french student in university. Also I love the city of Paris and it has been one of the best experiences in my life to live the parisian life for a semester.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I didn't get much information, but when I contacted the person responsible for the exchange students in my program, she very quickly set up a meeting and it was very easy to choose courses and begin. There was also a very good Erasmus event hosted by the university before study start , where we got a lot of information about the opportunities of social life for exchange students in Paris.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The only assistance I got was the meeting with Laurence Cathala who was the person responsible for the exchange students in the 'Life Science' program. Other than that I had to figure everything out myself including where all the classrooms were, where the lectures would take place, the amount of academic work required, how to prepare for exams ect.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Everyone was very kind and welcoming at Sorbonne Université and said that we could ask them questions if we had any, but other than the Erasmus event, we simply didn't get much practical information.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing in Fondation Danoise, which is the danish house in the campus Cité Universitaire. This was an amazing place to live and I can only recommend it! Very easy and nice way to meet a lot of other students, a lot of fun and interesting events and opportunities. 100% recommended.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's amazing if you find a student housing in Cité Universitaire, definitely don't be scared to find something off campus! Also Cité Universitaire is recommended by Sorbonne Université and they can help you with finding a student room.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got an email asking me to set up a meeting, and after that meeting I was registered in Moodle and in almost all my courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got an email asking me to set up a physical meeting, and after that meeting almost everything was registered. I wasn't registered in all my courses immediately and I had to email the administration a couple of times to make sure to be registered in everything.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administration for Erasmus students in my studies helped with registering during a physical meeting.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, the host university was very helpful in this proces.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact the administration right when you arrive and set up a meeting with them. They are very helpful with this.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the level of interesting subjects, but the burden of following all the courses were way heavier than indicated by the ECTS points and this unfortunately destroyed my profit of the courses in general.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think most of the professors were really intellectual and good speakers, but the big amount of work required to understand the courses and do well at exams was too big considered with the number of ECTS points for each course. This is especially relevant as I was following 8 different courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I attended to all the lectures and classes and tried to prepare for the classes as good as possible. Although we didn't receive any academic books and didn't get recommended pages to read for each lecture, which made it very hard to prepare for the lectures and also to prepare for the exams. In order to do well it was required that everything was understood immediately at the lectures, even though it was sometimes hard to hear the professor speak as the students sometimes spoke quite loudly at the same time as the professors.
In general I did not experience much structure and guidance in studying at Sorbonne Université and this was very hard for me as I am used to having my academic books to read in by myself and look in again for exam preparation. Also I experienced a lot of absence of information about exam dates and the format of the exams, which made it very difficult to be prepared and do well.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Bioinformatique
Tandem-R
Génétique
Neuro et Physiologie
Microbiologie
Maths et Stats
Biologie et Société
UE comp Langues: Français B1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend the language course in french. It is fun and gives a nice break from all the hard work.
Also I very much liked the course 'Biologie et Société' where you get to focus on a subject that you find interesting.
The course 'bioinformatique' in Python programming was also a very good introductory course, even though it was hard for me to do as well as I wanted to because of the work burden of other courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many kinds, you could find whatever interests you!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go out to eat, go to all the many markets and walk around a lot! Go to all the museums and see what you want to see from the beginning! The time is short, enjoy Paris!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Versailles, musée Rodin, musée du Louvre, Musée l'Orangérie, Musée d'Orsay. Go to the flea markets. Go to the speakeasy bars, ex. Lavomatic. Take long walks along la seine and spent evenings in Marais!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy as I love the french culture and language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them and be open from the beginning!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly the expectations in university.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language, the people reading in parks, the amazing bakeries with baguettes and many delicious cakes!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for the amount of academical work that is required from you. It is a lot and there's not much space to get behind.
Don't be afraid to contact the administration and/or teachers if you need help with anything!
Use the libraries and get help from the french students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most importantly I think you should be very aware of your level of french and if you are able to follow courses, because the way of studying in France is very different from how we do it in Denmark, so if your language is not good enough, it can become very very hard.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in Fondation Danoise in Cité Universitaire. I got friends for life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Following the courses and doing well at exams under the circumstances at the university.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
